verdict: KEEP(the variants) / CUT(the claim they are covered)

verdict: UNSURE(two competing reds, seven instances)
finding: Seven control boxes in the entire file carry an error border and six help texts are red — about 3.8% of the 183 field containers — and they are drawn in two different reds with no rule about which is correct.

verdict: KEEP(the rule) — it is honoured by zero form controls
finding: The library carries a written rule board saying a disabled control must say why via a tooltip; zero of the 198 form-control instances are disabled, and Tooltip[14:43] has one instance in the whole file — on the library page itself.

verdict: UNSURE(two field layouts, no rule for choosing)
finding: 183 field containers split 105 horizontal (label left, control right) / 52 vertical (label above) / 26 with no auto-layout — so the file has two field anatomies and 14% that are positioned by hand.

recommend: Make orientation an axis on the one Field component (Layout=stacked | inline) rather than a per-board decision, and set the rule: inline for settings rows with a short value, stacked wherever a help or error line can appear.

verdict: KEEP(the gaps are nearly consistent already)
finding: The label-to-control gap is 6px in 47 of 51 vertical fields (4px x3, 24px x1) and the control-to-help gap is 6px in 10 of 11 — the spacing is the ONE part of the field that is already a system, and it is exactly what a component would lock.

recommend: Ship 6px as the Field component's fixed internal gap and 16px as the inline variant's; the 4/12/24 outliers (6 nodes) are the whole cost of doing so.

verdict: CUT(the belief these are systematised)
finding: No sortable column header exists anywhere in the file — sorting is always a toolbar control above the list — pagination appears in at least four unrelated labellings with no component, and only 4 of 262 tables (1.5%) carry a row checkbox despite bulk-select being drawn as a screen state 105 times on page 1:3 alone.

Pagination: 'Next >' x12, 'Prev'/'Next ->' x1 each, 'Page 4' x1, 'Showing 200 of 412' x1, 'Showing resolved · 6' x2, 'Pagination' TEXT x2; no component. Bulk: name search for bulk/select all/multi-select returns 105 hits on 1:3 and 46 on 1:7, but the structural check (checkbox as a direct child of a table row) fires on 4 of 262 tables. The concept is also named three ways — 'Media · bulk-select', 'Pages · bulk-select', 'Layers · multi-select'.
recommend: Decide once whether tables sort by header or by toolbar and draw the losing option out; add a Select=on axis to Row[8:47] so bulk-select is a row capability instead of a separate screen; name the concept one way.

verdict: KEEP(place them)
finding: Five purpose-built list/table state components exist and are placed at most once each — the table loading skeleton is placed zero times — so 262 tables share one empty state, one error state and no loading state between them.
evidence: Instance counts: Dashboard/State — loading (table)[985:729] 0; — empty[985:682] 1; — error[985:694] 1; — denied[985:707] 1; — loading (list)[985:719] 1; Empty state[17:18] 1 (page 1:4). Against 262 detected tables and 1,026 Nav item instances, these are effectively unplaced.
recommend: Every table board needs its empty and loading twin, or the state components should be renamed as proposals. One instance of an empty state across 262 tables is the same shape of gap as a feature with no door.

screen: Dashboard v2 — 175 screens, zero Input instances
verdict: UNSURE(the newest page adopted the least)
finding: Page 988:2, the newest and second-largest product page, contains 0 instances of Input, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Toggle or Slider — every form control on 175 dashboard screens is a local frame, while the same page happily instances Dashboard/Nav item 251 times and Dashboard/Button 100 times.

verdict: UNSURE(the error variant cannot carry an error)
finding: Input[10:16]'s error variant is a red border around a single Placeholder text and nothing else — the component has no label, help or error slot at all, so a board that uses it cannot say what is wrong without hand-drawing the message beside it.
evidence: Screenshot of 10:16 read at source: five 240x42 boxes, states rest/focus/filled/error/disabled, distinguishable only by border colour and text colour. Inner composition of variant 10:6 read structurally: instances=0, localShapes=0, text=1 ('Placeholder'). That is why all 11 three-part fields in the file build their label and help as loose siblings.
recommend: This is the single strongest argument for the Field component in the proposal below — extending Input with slots would turn an atom into a molecule and break its 112 existing instances; wrapping it does not.

verdict: KEEP(code is ahead; do not implement backwards)
finding: The shipping code already gives every text input correct error styling for free via Tailwind's aria-invalid variant, including the focus-vs-invalid precedence — so the missing error boards are a design gap, not a build gap, and should not be treated as work for the editor package.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/textInputTheme.ts header: 'reproduced with Tailwind's built-in aria-invalid: variant instead of a color prop swap, so every plain call site gets correct error styling for free just by passing aria-invalid through' and 'reproduced exactly with an explicit aria-invalid:focus: compound variant'. Design side: 7 error-styled controls in 8 pages (D-P-05).
recommend: Mark any 'add error state' row as design-side. The code contract for error already exists; what is missing is a board that shows it, which is the founder's code-ahead escape hatch pointing the other way.
